question.problem: The solution to the inequality $-4x+5<-7$ is $x${{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $5$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4x+5 & <-7 \\ -4x+5-5 & <-7-5 \\ -4x+0 & <-12 \\ -4x & <-12\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-4.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4x\,\, & <\,\,-12 \\ \frac{-4x}{-4}\, & >\,\,\frac{-12}{-4} \\ \frac{\cancel{-4}x}{\cancel{-4}}\, & >\,\,3 \\ x\,\, & >\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x>3.$
